title: Electric vs Air Over Hydraulic Tube Bender Pump: Which Fits?

notes: The WebSearch budget for this session ran out before research on this article began, and the egress proxy blocks jd2.com, support.jd2.com and roguefab.com, so I could not open any page directly. Every number therefore comes from the WRITER-KIT known-good fact table or from docs/research/competitors-keywords-factcheck.md (which was itself compiled from search summaries). Eastwood air kit 90 psi and electric kit 0.75 HP / 110 V: kit fact table, from the Amazon listings. Eastwood High Capacity 2" x .120" mild / .090" 4130: kit fact table. JD2 Model 32 (manual limit 2" x .120", 2" x .250" DOM with hydraulics, 10-ton cylinder recommended): kit fact table. Fact-check notes only, so please re-verify: Rogue Fab M605 offered with manual hydraulic, air-over-hydraulic or 1.5 / 2.0 HP electric-hydraulic power; M625 'as M605'; about 94 degrees per ram stroke (also in the kit table). Pro-Tools 105HD hydraulic package with a 10-ton cylinder. Left out as unverifiable: air consumption (CFM) for any pump, amp draw, duty cycle, voltage of Rogue Fab's electric units, pump speed in degrees per second, Woodward Fab WFB2-AHP air specs, and any 220 V requirement for a specific product. The power table marks these as 'confirm with the maker' instead of guessing. Statements that 110 V is the usual US household voltage, and the general advice on extension cords and circuits, are qualitative general knowledge.
